label: Orbital Salvage contracts
_comment: The proof that the engine reads declarations rather than vocabulary. Nothing here is a fantasy noun: the pool is Charge, the damage types are kinetic and thermal, the components roll under their own property prefix, and the weapon and vest ride attack/defense profiles like any other set's. See docs/design/cross_theme_engine_contracts.md.

stats._comment: This set keeps the engine's stat vocabulary, but says so rather than relying on the fallback -- that is the difference between a set that has been checked and one that happens to work. `power` drives charge, and `evasion` is the skill this set's stat_bonuses names. `ability_power` and `resistance` name stats this set actually carries: left to the engine's fallback they would have read `spell_power` and `magic_resist`, which no orbital entity has, so both mechanics would have sat at the neutral default and never moved. `ability_power` rides the same stat as the charge pool because one stat driving both is what a salvage rig's aptitude means here. `resistance` names `insulation` -- a small derived rating, the shape `magic_resist` has in fantasy (2), NOT a core attribute: the flat reduction is the stat's raw value, so pointing this role at `constitution` would subtract 10 from every energy hit and make the hold's frost harmless. Crew carry a little; the salvager carries none and survives the cold on gear, which is what this set's vest is for.

attack_profiles._comment: `damage_type` is the channel resistance maths uses; `weapon_damage_type` is the material-interaction axis. A synthetic vest declares no material multiplier, so this lands unmodified.

work.label: Running a patch-kit batch
work.description: Feed the bay three parts and let it work slowly. It wastes less than hands do: two kits from three parts, where the bench recipe gets one from two. Half a day, and it is done whether or not anyone is standing there.
